summary: Iter 7 e2e testing PASSED. Backend: 42/42 pytest tests passing (26 regression + 16 new for auth + intake + extraction). All 3 auth endpoints validate correctly: POST /api/auth/session returns 400 on empty session_id, 422 on missing field, and 401/502 on bogus id; GET /api/auth/me returns 401 for guests and the seeded user for both Bearer token and cookie; POST /api/auth/logout deletes the session doc. All 3 intake endpoints work: GET /api/intake/{sid} returns {session_id, fields:{}} for unknown session; PATCH merges fields with deep-dotted $set and whitelists INTAKE_FIELDS; POST /submit requires name+phone, writes appointments row with source='ai_intake', returns logged_in:false for guest and logged_in:true with user_id when Bearer token is present. Assistant extraction: 'Hi my name is Jane Smith, my mom needs help after hip surgery' produced extracted.name='Jane Smith' plus condition/caregiver fields and persisted to db.intakes so subsequent GET /api/intake/{sid} reflected them. Frontend: Header shows 'Sign in' (data-testid='auth-login-btn') on Home and /ai; Home testimonials render (4 cards). /ai welcome chip 'Start my intake' transitions to IntakeView with all 10 labeled fields + progress bar + guest banner containing [data-testid=intake-signin-btn] which triggers navigation on click. Sending 'My name is Jane Smith and I have hip pain' via chat-input auto-populated intake-input-name='Jane Smith' and intake-input-condition='hip pain' within ~15s (progress jumped to 20%). Manually filling phone+service revealed 'Submit & request appointment' button; clicking it produced <canvas> (confetti) + toast. AuthCallback route: navigating to /profile#session_id=fake-session-id-12345 was detected synchronously by AppRouter, POST to /api/auth/session fired (got 401 from OAuth provider for bogus id), and cleanly redirected to /ai — hash-based routing works.

issues: Preferred-contact-time field in IntakeWizard is a plain text <input> rather than a time/date picker or the shadcn Calendar used elsewhere. It will accept any string (my test inadvertently typed 'Hip pain' into it). Consider semantic type='time' or a Calendar component.
Carryover from iter 6: dyn-appointment-form still uses browser's native date picker instead of shadcn Calendar.

action_items: (Optional/minor) Backend test for /api/auth/session test_invalid_session_id_returns_401 currently accepts 401 OR 502 because Emergent OAuth provider may be unreachable from test env. If provider becomes stable, tighten to 401-only.
(Optional/minor) Preferred-contact-time field in IntakeWizard accepts free-form strings — consider input[type=time] or shadcn Calendar.
(Carryover) dyn-appointment-form native date picker vs shadcn Calendar for brand consistency.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to 629 lines — nearing the 700-line threshold. Recommend splitting into modules: auth.py (User model + /auth routes + get_current_user), intake.py (Intake routes + INTAKE_FIELDS), assistant.py (SYSTEM_PROMPT + /assistant routes), models.py (Contact/Referral/Survey/Appointment), main.py (FastAPI app + router wiring). Not blocking.
get_current_user correctly handles both httpOnly cookie AND Authorization: Bearer header, excludes _id via projection, parses ISO string expires_at with tz-safe comparison — clean and testable.
submit_intake persists user_id only when session is valid (guest-first design), and appointment.source='ai_intake' makes downstream filtering trivial. Good.
PATCH /intake/{sid} whitelists INTAKE_FIELDS before $set, preventing arbitrary field injection — security-correct.
assistant_chat auto-merges extracted fields into db.intakes via deep-dotted $set keyed by session_id, so the same chat sessionId is reusable as the intake sessionId in the frontend. Elegant contract.
Frontend chat-input data-testid present (confirmed via DOM scan). IntakeWizard exposes intake-signin-btn, intake-input-name, intake-input-condition — all data-testid-compliant.
Previously-reported 2x ChatPanel mount (desktop + mobile stacked) is unchanged; still causes 2x GET /assistant/history on mount. Low-priority.

401s from /api/auth/me on guest page load are expected (AuthProvider fires /me on mount). They appear as red console noise; consider swallowing 401 as a non-error state in the Axios/fetch interceptor.
